title: The segmented control's thumb is lighter than its rail and moves as Liquid Glass
goal: User 2026-09-29: 'I think the segmented control's thumb should be lighter than the rail, and ideally, should use liquid glass animation effect when snapping between options.' The shared control is Sources/Photonz/DesignSystem/SegmentedControl.swift (built to comp-segmented.html). This is the user's own change to their component, so update the component page docs/design/mocks/pages/comp-segmented.html first (with a comment citing this request) and the app to match. Use the platform's Liquid Glass (macOS 26: glassEffect on the thumb inside a GlassEffectContainer, glassEffectID with a namespace so the thumb morphs between segments), not a hand-drawn imitation.
acceptance: The thumb is clearly visible at a glance (user 2026-09-29: 'I can barely see the thumb atm'): measured on the rendered control in light and dark, over the title bar and over the panel, the thumb-to-rail contrast is at least 1.5:1 and the thumb has a hairline edge or soft shadow that separates it from the rail; photographs of each placement in the audit

comp-segmented.html shows the thumb lighter than the rail in light and dark (a contrast the eye reads at once, measured in the audit: thumb vs rail luminance), and the snap animation described and demonstrated as best HTML can

In the app the thumb is a Liquid Glass shape inside a GlassEffectContainer on a darker rail; choosing another segment morphs the glass across with the system's glass spring (stretching toward the target and settling), interruptible mid-flight, with no cross-fade or jump
Dragging the thumb across segments tracks the pointer and snaps with the same glass motion on release
Reduce Motion replaces the morph with a quick cross-fade; Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency give an opaque lighter thumb
Every use (View | Edit in the title bar and every panel segmented picker) gets it, since they share the control
A short screen recording or a sequence of 6+ frames of the morph goes in the audit next to the updated component page, and a card asks the user to judge the feel

log.note: User 2026-09-29: can barely see the thumb today. Contrast is now a hard acceptance item; moved to the front.

Intake window updated the component page and shared CSS/JS (605a5c4a + this): recessed rail, lighter glass thumb tokens (--seg-rail, --seg-thumb*), and the stretch-squash-spring morph (420ms). Build the app control to match that page; the mock half of acceptance item 2 is done.

User 2026-09-29: the overshoot was obnoxious on multi-step moves (it left the rail). Page fixed in 85a035e7: settle is a fixed min(3px, 6% of travel), clamped inside the rail, no distance-proportional spring. The app morph must follow the same rule: the thumb never leaves the rail and never overshoots by more than a few points, however far it moves.

Also from the mock: never animate a thumb's position and size on different paths (transform vs frame). In WebKit they desynced and the thumb left the rail. The SwiftUI morph must move frame and size as one animation.
